question: Q5

statements.why: NVIDIA's fiscal Q2 sales to the largest cloud companies, $49B and up 13% on the quarter, fit roughly $800B of big-five capex; rung 3 stands.
The same fact from another outlet: $48.71B hyperscale revenue, up 117%. It confirms strong spending in 2026 but sizes no capex outside the $750-850B band.

why: Only NVIDIA's own hyperscaler sales bear on this question, and they fit the nearly $800B reference. Broadcom and Trainium figures are too indirect to size big-five data-center capex.

question: Q12
why: No statement mentions CPO switches, optical networking units or NVIDIA networking revenue. Rubin ramp, revenue and margin figures say nothing about 2027 CPO switch volume.

question: Q13

statements.why: Broadcom AI semiconductor revenue was $10.8B in Q2, up 143%: about $43B a year from one supplier, which makes below $40B unlikely even after networking.
Broadcom's Q3 AI guidance of $16.0B is about a $64B annual run-rate. Mostly custom accelerators, it points to calendar-2026 spending of $40-80B.
Trainium at multi-billion-dollar scale adds unquantified custom-silicon spending. Alone it would not cross $40B, but it weakens confidence in below $40B.
The Broadcom ramp for Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI starts late 2026 and runs into 2027. It adds little to the calendar-2026 amount.
A 27% growth rate through 2033 with no base-year level cannot place 2026 spending on the ladder.

why: The request quantified no 2026 spending at all. Broadcom's reported and guided AI revenue alone suggests roughly $40B or more, likely moving the answer above below-$40B.

question: Q2
